headline: Weak fertilizer demand weighs on earnings; subsidy revision to support recovery

highlights: Modest revenue growth offset by sharp margin contraction  CRIN reported overall revenue of INR103b (est. 93b) in 2QFY27, up ~7% YoY.

Nutrient & other allied business revenue grew 4% YoY to INR90.4b, with crop protection business revenue growing 22% YoY to ~INR13.1b.  Total manufacturing fertilizer volumes (NPK + DAP) declined 38% YoY to 665kmt, and total phosphate fertilizer manufacturing volumes (including SSP) declined 34% to 859kmt.
Overall phosphatic volumes (NPK + DAP) declined by 30% to 991kmt.

According to our calculations, manufacturing EBITDA/MT (including SSP) declined 8% YoY to INR5,861, while EBITDA/MT for phosphate fertilizers (DAP and NPK) stood at INR7,206 (-3% YoY).  EBITDA margin contracted 270bp YoY to 9.2% (est. 9.6%).
valuation: The 0.75m MT Kakinada granulation facility is targeted for commissioning by Feb’27, with full utilization in FY28.  Subsidy: CRIN received INR44.78b in subsidy during 1HFY27, with an additional INR12b received in Oct’26; receivables stood at INR35.35b as of Sep’26.

Valuation and view  We expect CRIN to face near-term challenges in the fertilizers segment due to subdued consumption and volatile raw material costs, although revised Rabi subsidy rates and higher captive acid utilization should support recovery in 2HFY27.
Management described nano-product margins as healthy but did not provide a numerical margin or contribution target.
watch: Fertilizer demand, pricing, inventory and backward integration  Fertilizer demand was affected by deficient rainfall across key markets, rupee depreciation, elevated raw material prices and Kharif subsidy rates that did not adequately compensate for higher manufacturing costs.  Industry DAP and NPK sales totaled 10.4m MT in 1HFY27 vs. 12.1m MT in 1HFY26.
It also discussed a possible correction below USD500/MT, although this remained a conditional view rather than firm guidance; renewed increases in ammonia prices remained a concern.
